lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p30 - Talk about the chart.

details: Talk about the chart introduces data interpretation. Students examine the bar chart image to understand how the height of the coloured bars corresponds to the number of children on the axis.
Look for students pointing to the tallest bar (Bus) or the shortest bar (Bicycle) and reading the corresponding numbers on the left.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p30 - Listen, point and say.

details: Listen, point and say reinforces the data extraction skills. Students listen to questions like "How many children walk?" and answer by reading the chart.
Look for accurate tracking of the red 'Walk' bar to the number '7' in the photo example and stating the number clearly.

details: Ask and answer checks data comprehension verbally. Students interpret their written data by answering questions like "How many cars?"
Look for quick retrieval of the information, like "Five cars" or "Eight buses."

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p30 - 3. Try it out! Do a class survey.

details: Do a class survey applies the concept to real life. Students ask their classmates "How do you go to school?" and record the answers to create their own class data set.
Look for active participation in asking questions and recording answers (using tally marks or blocks) on a shared or individual sheet.

lessonPlan.topic: Numbers Book p107 - Continue the pattern. Draw and colour.

details: Continue the pattern develops logical reasoning. Students identify the repeating sequence of shape and colour (e.g., Red Triangle, Green Square) and draw the next items in the row.
Look for correct identification of the pattern rules (AB, AB...) and drawing the correct shape in the correct colour to finish the line.
